title: With a hard pair, class-(K) counting is #P-hard with H1 = Z/r: the dichotomy
claim: for p odd, r | p - 1 and G = N x| C_r of class (K), if G has a hard pair then counting homomorphisms from pi1 of r-surgeries on knots (H1 = Z/r), given by diagrams, to G is #P-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions (at most r oracle calls per value of a fixed Bulatov-Grohe partition function): the construction of COPRIME-CLASS2-20261026-001D section 3 realizes the gadget manifolds of CLASSK-DICHOTOMY-20261026-001A for all three slot patterns, the count is a positive sum of multiplicative sector partition functions, an anchor graph and a Vandermonde solve over disjoint unions isolate the hard sector, and Bulatov-Grohe applies to its positive weight matrix of rank at least two. With COPRIME-CLASS2-20261026-001C this is a dichotomy for closed 3-manifolds with |H1| <= C: polynomial iff no G_d (d | r, d <= C) has a hard pair. The same holds for knot groups (at most r|B| calls), also when commutators involve the trivial character: the u-pairing is unchanged by the moves and block-diagonal over the base summands, so the knot count is a positive sum of multiplicative terms indexed by (k, beta). Hence Rowell's Conjecture 3.2(b) fails for every class-(K) group with a hard pair over odd prime fields unless every #P function is polynomial-time computable.
failure_conditions: A hard pair whose sector-1 weight is constant, not positive, or of rank one.
A group with no hard pair and a nonconstant sector weight for some slot triple.

A concrete group for which no anchor among small multigraphs separates sector 1 from the sectors that differ from it, or for which the Vandermonde solve does not return (sum over I of c_k) f_1(Gamma).
A disjoint union on which a sector term is not the product of its parts (model or measured surgeries).

On the extended knot-exterior model, a sector where the sum over beta of the fixed-beta counts differs from the knot count, where the beta = 0 term differs from the closed count, or where a fixed-beta count is not multiplicative.
Measured knot-exterior counts on K2 + K2 that differ from the sum over beta of the squared fixed-beta counts on K2.
A restricted subgroup G_d whose hard pairs differ from the stated refinement examples.
foundation_claim_scope: Odd prime fields with r | p - 1, closed orientable 3-manifolds with bounded first homology (triangulations, balanced presentations or knot surgeries) and knot groups; Turing reductions. Cited, not reproved: Bulatov-Grohe (as stated in Cai-Chen-Lu, Theorem 2.1), the realization of COPRIME-CLASS2-20261026-001D section 3 (Habiro, Massuyeau through COPRIME-CLASS2-20261026-001B), COPRIME-CLASS2-20261026-001B (c) and (d), COPRIME-CLASS2-20261026-001C. Not covered: p = 2, extension fields, groups outside class (K), approximate counting. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: Bulatov-Grohe hypotheses for 94 hard pairs (63 ranks computed, 7 too large to tabulate with the pairing criterion checked) and 576 negative cases; anchors and exact Vandermonde recovery on four groups including two equivalent hard sectors; the knot-exterior decomposition over beta on the extended model for five fixture-group pairs with multiplicativity; end to end on the frozen experiment rows, closed counts on K2 + K2 equal squares and knot counts equal sums over beta of squares for eight groups; the refinement by subgroup orders; size data; no human or external review
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-26.
